fact_check.claim: 'Kaspa hasn't really retraced too much... it's up nine percent on a 24 hour chart, that's amazing... could it go down? Yeah, of course, if Bitcoin goes down everything else goes down... just yesterday it was down 3.7 which isn't too low all things considered compared to how it was over the last few months' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: numbers UPDATED. $KAS $0.0413, about a $1.14B cap, rank 73, +4.4% 24h, -0.5% 7d, -1.2% 14d, +15.2% 30d; ATH $0.2074 on July 31, 2024, so about 80% under it. Over the same 7 days: $BTC -2.4%, $TAO -5.8%, $TON -2.7%, Cash Cat -33%, so 'flat on the week while everything else bled' holds. Copy uses 'about 4.1 cents', 'flat on the week', 'up about 15% on the month' and never the on-stream 9% (it was +4.4% at drafting time). The 'if Bitcoin dumps, could it? Of course' line is Mike's own.

fact_check.claim: 'I think TAO is on a steal right now... long term I think TAO is going to be absolutely insanely high... AI is a whole narrative and there's no better play than TAO when it comes to AI'; the $326 sell, the $290 target and the $302 buy-back (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: price UPDATED and the trade history NOT repeated. $TAO $272.02, about a $3.08B cap, rank 38, -5.8% 7d, -11.5% 14d, +3.9% 30d; ATH $757.60 on March 7, 2024, so about 64% under it. 'A steal' and 'no better AI play' are Mike's own conviction, written in first person. The $326 / $302 bull-trap story already shipped on 2026-10-03 (the bull-trap batch tweet, poll and thread) and would read as a timing regret, so it is left out; the tweet is forward-looking only. persona project_handles tao = null, so no Follow line. Whisper's lowercase Greek-letter mishear of TAO corrected everywhere.

fact_check.claim: 'Meme coin dominance in the market has dropped considerably since 2024, falling off a cliff... it's us trading against ourselves, no new market participants... a lot of these memes don't even last a week'; 'I was meme coins only in 2024 and then moved on to utility projects and we did a huge amount of multipliers' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost (Oct 5, 2026): meme coins are roughly 3% of total altcoin market cap, versus above 10% during the November 2024 meme season (3.7% in July 2026, about 3.2% in late 2025); meme coin holder counts at multi-year lows. CryptoRank: the sector fell 81.9% from its November 2024 peak of $135.06B to $24.48B on June 15, 2026; CoinDCX had it near $31.2B in September 2026, so copy says 'roughly 80% below its $135B peak'. New centralized-exchange meme listings fell from 196 in Q4 2024 to 41 in Q2 2026. 'Us trading against ourselves', 'dead by day five' and the 2024 meme-only to utility pivot are Mike's own reads; copy writes 'altcoin market' (the CryptoQuant ratio is a share of altcoins, not of total crypto).

fact_check.claim: 'Look what happened with Dynamite, it just rugged out of nowhere after a few days... really well built out website... the Twitter is already dead, everything is deleted' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: UNVERIFIED: no coverage of a 'Dynamite' meme rug could be found, so the token is NOT named and no specific event is claimed. Copy keeps the general form only ('some come with a fully built-out website and a real content push, and still rug within days: site gone, X account gone, everything deleted'), which depends on nothing but the pattern Mike described.
fact_check.source: web search (no result for the token); transcript

fact_check.claim: 'Ledger users getting drained, reported losses reaching 90 million dollars'; 'it wasn't Ledger's fault, all those Ledgers were bought from another site, not directly from Ledger... a long con... whenever you buy a hardware wallet buy directly from the actual vendor... same thing with phones' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified with the figure CORRECTED. Oct 9, 2026: Ledger is investigating wallet drains involving customers of CryptoBilis, an official reseller in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines; on-chain estimates run from about $72M to $86.9M across 98 addresses, and Ledger has not confirmed a total, so copy says 'about $86M', never $90M. Ledger said its own infrastructure was not compromised, asked CryptoBilis to pause all sales and shipments, and advised anyone who bought in the past 90 days not to start setup and to consider moving assets to a new signer. Changpeng Zhao suggested a supply-chain attack with tampered or counterfeit devices; copy calls that 'the working theory'. 'A long con' and the buy-direct rule are Mike's own. OPERATOR FLAG: a developing story; re-check the loss figure before the Ledger tweet goes out.

fact_check.claim: 'I'm saying we're going down to 74, complete this M pattern, maybe in a couple days and probably quickly recover... we're below the 50-week moving average and we'll quickly come above it and use it as support'; 'I would like to speak to the CEO of October... it's not really happening yet, it happened in the last week of September, we got to get down first before we can go back up'; 'Bitcoin could go down another 8K at least' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own call, with the moving-average read CORRECTED and the September run verified. $BTC $82,407 on 2026-10-09 (-2.4% 7d, +4.9% 30d, ATH $126,080 on Oct 6, 2025). Coinbase daily closes: Sept 15 $75,584 to Sept 21 $86,595, a +14.6% run in six days, which is the 'Uptober printed in the last week of September' line; October opened at $83,556 and sits about 1.4% red month-to-date. The 50-week SMA computed from the last 50 completed weekly closes is about $77.7K, so Bitcoin is ABOVE it, not below as read on stream; copy therefore never says 'below the 50-week SMA' and does not use the moving average at all. The $74K dip target, the M pattern and 'gets gobbled up fast' are Mike's own and are written in first person. The bull-trap and 'maybe toward $75K' versions shipped on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-05, so this batch carries the call only as one single-line tweet with the new $74K level and the CEO-of-October joke.
fact_check.source: api.exchange.coinbase.com/products/BTC-USD/candles (daily, 600 rows to 2026-10-09; 50-week SMA computed from weekly closes); api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/markets?ids=bitcoin; repurpose/output/bull-trap-lane3-plan.json and grapes-lane3-plan.json; transcript

fact_check.claim: 'There's more QE, there's more injections of dollars into the economy today, and as we know one of that flows first into crypto' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: CORRECTED and NOT used. The Oct 8, 2026 New York Fed operation was a scheduled reinvestment purchase of about $3.9B in Treasury bills already on the desk's published calendar, not new quantitative easing; the Fed had paused additional reserve-management purchases through the period ending Oct 14, and net liquidity was pressured by a $47.4B rise in the Treasury General Account. No copy mentions QE or a liquidity injection.

fact_check.claim: 'Turbo is one of them, a little bit bigger cult meme, 66 million'; 'another one of my favorites is Housecoin, I haven't checked it recently but I would imagine very active team, non-stop content'; cult memes named: lo-fi, Wojak, Rage Guy, Troll, Pepe, Toshi, Doginme, Keycat; 'Bitty: 17 million is all time high and one million right now, even 10 million would be a 10x' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Turbo verified and featured: $TURBO about a $66.7M cap (matches the on-stream 66M), rank 389, -5% 7d, about 93% under its December 2024 ATH, a 2023 launch; persona says engage in-tribe, Follow: @TurboToadToken is the closing line (mention-triggered handle). Housecoin DROPPED from copy: $HOUSE sits at about a $738K cap, 99.4% under its April 2025 ATH (past Mike's own 97% rug line) and the 'active team' remark was hedged on stream ('I haven't checked it recently'), so it fails verified-claims-only as a featured subject (OPERATOR FLAG: Housecoin is in the persona stacking lineup; Mike may want to speak to it himself). Pepe, Toshi and Doginme are named in the YT post body only, with cashtags, as Mike's own list of cult memes; no handle lines there. Bitty (The Bitcoin Mascot, $BITTY) checks out roughly ($1.3M cap, about 94% under its Sept 2025 ATH) but is not named; the 10x-without-a-new-ATH math is written in general form ('a cult meme at 5% of its old high').

fact_check.claim: Mike's AI-and-robots video thesis repeated on stream: 'everybody's job is at risk... the combined knowledge of every expert electrician in the world in your robot... self-driving trucks... it could be illegal for humans to drive... you gotta own assets: water, energy, compute power, real estate, food, recreation, health and biotech... technology is deflationary, the money supply is inflationary, crypto helps answer that... a few years ago it would have cost you like two thousand Bitcoin to buy a house, now a couple'; a viewer: 'they told you to learn to code, then AI learned to code' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own thesis (persona core_theses: the AI buildout, and TAO as the AI inference layer with KAS as the PoW money layer, which the post uses as its crypto beat). The house math is ANCHORED: NAR's 2013 annual median existing-home price was $197,100 and Bitcoin first crossed $100 in the spring of 2013 (late March / April 1), so about 2,000 BTC; NAR's August 2026 median was $429,100 and $BTC was $82,407 on 2026-10-09, so about 5.2 BTC, written 'about five'. 'Human driving could end up illegal' softens the on-stream 'it's going to be illegal' to Mike's conditional. The video's view counts (574 vs 4,300) are self-undermining and NOT used; the YT post points to 'my latest video' and 'the full breakdown on the channel' with cta_target subscribe_youtube (the brief's 'no longform video' means Lane 1 is skipped for this batch, not that the existing video cannot be referenced).
fact_check.source: nar.realtor/newsroom (2013 annual median $197,100, Jan 23, 2014 release) via mortgagenewsdaily.com/news/01232014-existing-home-sales; nar.realtor/newsroom/nar-existing-home-sales-report-shows-2-0-decrease-in-august (Aug 2026 median $429,100); coinpedia.org (13 years since Bitcoin first hit $100) and siliconangle.com (April 3, 2013); api.coingecko.com (bitcoin); persona.json core_theses; transcript

fact_check.claim: Dropped from the batch: the AI-generated Susan Dell / Megan Fox / Obama videos going around X; Trump's 'big announcement' on diesel prices, the AI-to-SI rename, the Iran attack timing, the 28 million barrels of oil and the 'Don-Zoo: wars are only fought on the weekend' meme; Eliza's dead-cat bounce; Golden Kitty 'hanging in there below the 886' and Swole 'should be higher'; SPON at a tiny cap with the devs quiet for 48 hours; the Michigan consumer sentiment print; CPI on Oct 14 and PPI on Oct 15; the SUI higher-low lesson (64 cents never came back, the 0.618 at 72 cents); LCX, Arbitrum, Canton, Bitcoin Cash, Near, BNB under 800; Uncle's missing CoinMarketCap listing; We Love Cats versus the cat memes; Plumber on Base; the viewer's Handle fumble; the Pippin 89x story; PerpsPad 114x; the crypto community pitch; the Cash Cat / Swole Cat origin lore
fact_check.verdict: not drafted. The deepfake videos and every Trump line are political and personal tangents that persona reserves for Mike to post himself. Eliza is banned content. Golden Kitty and Swole are Mike's own calls now deep underwater (CoinGecko on 2026-10-09: $GOLDEN about a $492K cap, -86% on the week, 92% under its Sept 27 ATH; $SWOLE about a $70K cap, -80% on the week) and SPON already shipped, so all three stay out (OPERATOR FLAG: Golden Kitty fell hard after the Oct 5 batch; Mike may want to address it himself). The Michigan print (Oct 9: 46.3 headline, a five-month low; current conditions 44.7, expectations 47.3 beating the 45.5 forecast; 1-year inflation expectations 4.7%) and the CPI / PPI dates are verified but stale by post time and were left out. The SUI walk-through is trader-portfolio framing. LCX, Arbitrum, Canton, BCH, Near and BNB were lukewarm passing takes, Uncle and We Love Cats are negative reads on named tokens that could not be verified, Plumber and Handle are chat throwaways, Pippin ($PIPPIN now 98% under its Feb 2026 ATH) and PerpsPad ride with the community pitch (membership pitch; the Pippin story also opens on a missed first leg). The Cash Cat origin story is VERIFIED (Vlad Tenev's April 14, 2021 post said the app was almost called Cash Cat, with the buff-cat meme attached; $CASHCAT launched on Robinhood Chain in July 2026) but was cut for space behind the six default tweet slots; it is a ready-made optional item if Mike wants it (Vlad-Tenev.webp, cash-cat.jpg and swole.png exist as references).

yt_posts.body:
Meme coins are about 3% of the altcoin market right now. In November 2024 they were over 10%.

I pulled up the meme coin dominance chart on stream this week and it was an eye opener: the whole sector is falling off a cliff. Here is what that number changes about how I pick memes, and the one filter I still trust.

Start with the size of the hole. The entire meme sector peaked at about $135B in November 2024 and has lost roughly 80% of that. Meme coin holder counts are at multi-year lows. New exchange listings for memes went from 196 in the last quarter of 2024 to 41 in the second quarter of this year. That is not a dip, that is the crowd leaving.

And it explains what I see on the charts every week. There is no new money in memes right now. It is us trading against ourselves: the same wallets buying from each other, with nobody new walking through the door. A new launch pumps for a day or two and dies by day five. Some of them come with a fully built-out website and a real content push, and still rug within days: site gone, X account gone, everything deleted. A lot of these do not even last a week.

So here is where I landed. I am done with brand-new launches in this market. The only memes I touch are the cult memes: the ones that already survived a full cycle, still have a team shipping and still have real exchange listings. Turbo ($TURBO) is one of them, a 2023 meme still sitting at about a $67M cap. Pepe ($PEPE), Toshi ($TOSHI), Doginme ($DOGINME): that whole class has already been through the fire.

And the math on cult memes is different. A cult meme sitting at 5% of its old high does not need a new all-time high to pay you; half way back to the old high is a 10x. A brand-new launch under a $1M cap is a shot in the dark. The odds it ever sees $5M are tiny, and $50M or $100M is rarer still.

One more thing. In 2024 I was meme-only, and I am glad I moved on to utility plays too, because that is where a lot of our biggest multipliers came from. A meme-only mentality in a market where memes are 3% of alts is fighting over a shrinking pie.

When new money finally comes back into crypto, it is not coming back for the launch of the week. Never financial advice.

Tell me in the comments: name the ONE meme you think is still alive when the new money shows up next year, and why that one.

Click that like button and click the subscribe button if you want the meme reads before the crowd shows up.

yt_posts.body:
AI and robots are coming for every job. Not the factory jobs; those went first. Every job.

Imagine the combined knowledge of every expert electrician on Earth loaded into one robot. Now do that for plumbers, carpenters, roofers, truck drivers, accountants, coders. Here is why I think the only real protection is to own assets, and which ones.

In my latest video I went down the list and I could not find a job that is safe. The first wave of automation went after muscle: the factory floor, the assembly line. This wave goes after knowledge work and the skilled trades at the same time. They told you to learn to code; then AI learned to code. Self-driving trucks are coming for the truckers in my chat, and the day self-driving cars stop crashing, human driving could end up illegal.

I do not know what the world looks like in five years. It might be rough for some people and not for others, and the line between the two is going to be simple: do you own assets, or do you only own a paycheck?

Because here is the good news hiding inside this. Technology is deflationary. Everything a robot makes gets cheaper, so if you own less, you can do more with less. The problem is that money is not deflationary. There is no free market in the money supply; it only ever inflates, and that is what makes life harder every year. Crypto is the answer to that half of the problem. In the spring of 2013 a median American home cost about 2,000 Bitcoin. This week it costs about five.

So own assets, and choose them wisely. Anything to do with water, energy and compute power. Real estate. Food. Health and biotech. And crypto, where I stay with the two neutral layers nobody owns: $TAO as the AI inference layer and $KAS as the proof-of-work money layer. The more governments and corporations race to control compute, money and AI, the more those two are worth.

Get in while you still have the paycheck. Dollar-cost average into the big ones, learn to time the tops and bottoms along the way, and build the size of your bag. Never financial advice.

Tell me in the comments: if AI takes the paycheck, which asset class holds up best: real estate, energy, compute, or crypto?
